summary: Watsa territory (Haut-Uele) is mostly state-held: Watsa-Durba, the Kibali gold mine area, Gombari, Giro and Moku are run by police and administration with FARDC present, and northern/central areas see only banditry on mining sites. Since early 2026 the ADF/ISCAP has expanded north from Mambasa into the forests of the south, setting up a stronghold at Suka na Mboka in Kebo chefferie; FARDC clashed with them in April 2026 and run sweep operations. More than 10,000 people fled the Kebo-Apodo, Andobi and Mahaa chefferies toward Mungbere, Gombari, Watsa and Moku. The southern Apodo/Nepoko fringe is assessed as contested between FARDC and ADF; Mungbere is an FARDC operations hub.

zones.description: Watsa-Durba urban area (Watsa centre, Durba/Kibali mine town and neighbourhoods Toyota, Bethanie, Doko, Durba, Gatanga)
zones.evidence: Territorial seat and Kibali gold mine hub, functioning normally (Kibali community programmes Sept 2026) and receiving people displaced by the ADF in mid-2026, i.e. state-held. Civil society complained in Jan 2026 of armed bandit attacks on nearby mining sites, which are criminal raids rather than territorial control.

zones.description: Rural Watsa health zone (Kokoro, Dubele, Ngangazo, Monya, Gatanga, Moku, Maitulu, Arumbi, Dilolo etc.) and Akua/Nzopi villages
zones.evidence: No armed-group territorial control reported in northern and central Watsa; insecurity consists of armed robberies on artisanal mining sites. Moku received ADF displaced in 2026. Assigned to state police by default.

zones.description: Gombari secteur north and centre (Gombari, Wanga, Goria/Giro, Tora, Madja, Ngazizi, Tibodri, Toli)
zones.evidence: Gombari and Giro are cited as 'more secure agglomerations' receiving displaced from the ADF-affected south in 2026; no armed-group control reported. FARDC reinforcements transit on the RN26.

zones.description: Andobi chefferie: Mungbere (GRID3 'Salongo', Tangi) and Bakiri/Baitebi area
zones.evidence: Mungbere, capital of Andobi chefferie, is a reception point for displaced and the base for FARDC sweep operations against the ADF launched in 2026 with movement restrictions; ADF alerts and raids nearby (Apodo, March 2026) but the town remains government-held.

zones.description: Southern forest fringe: Apodo, Nepoko and Abakudu health areas (Kebo-Apodo chefferie, toward Suka na Mboka) and Kaungato (Nduye side)
zones.evidence: The ADF established a stronghold at Suka na Mboka in Kebo chefferie (forest between Mambasa, Wamba and Watsa); FARDC clashed with them there on 30 April 2026 and conduct sweep operations. Over 10,000 people fled Kebo-Apodo, Andobi and Mahaa; villages are largely emptied and army-held positions face ADF incursions.
